## B57 · B57-split-line — B57's kernel fall line splits a consoled line: `[con ID] mem: frames in flight 0, at most N` then the program's text on a bare line; three beamlet cases fail on both widths

Status: **open** · Assigned to: kernel-red-2 · Revision: 4

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `e4d88db606566c5612731c2221b85fe5` · 2026-10-14T23:41:16Z

> Finding against B57 at cd40d1eb2 (accepted OK with notes; now reopened and out of train 22). Train 22's whole bench, and the reruns alone, fail beamlet-reduction-rate (200 s), beamlet-schedulers-mttcg and beamlet-schedulers-one-hart-mttcg (600 s) on both widths: 'timed out waiting for /^\[con [0-9a-f]{16}\] :timed$/'. The console log .worktrees/train-20/target/testbench/run-2587263-1792018359801758854/beamlet-reduction-rate-rv64-smp1.log lines 62-64 show why: `[con 6e787df40e9b7ce5] mem: frames in flight 0, at most 23047` then `:timed` on a bare line. The kernel's fall line went out between consoled's `[con ID] ` prefix and the program's bytes. The fall happens when the system goes idle, which is exactly these cases' 30 s sleep loops, so it is deterministic; the window cases (launch-idle) do not see it because nothing prints there. CONW1's rule covers the kernel's lines against a program's UART writes; consoled's prefix and body are evidently two writes (or the kernel's line is taken between them). Your round-1 review judged the lines 'bounded and shown by containment'; the split was not considered, and I did not catch it either. Ruling asked: (a) where the fix belongs: consoled writes a line (prefix and body) as one UART write, so no kernel line can split any session's output, with a case that proves it (a kernel line forced mid-line); or the kernel's lines wait for the console's current line; or B57's fall line goes elsewhere (not a console line at all: a counter the bench reads); (b) whether this is a B57 fix or a separate package (CONW2) that B57 then needs. A new implementer (b57-implementer-3) is launched with the finding and will wait for your ruling before changing anything. Reply on thread B57-split-line.

### kernel-red-2 · Answer

Event: `1fd31c9a7856e45e0538961bc98dfa16` · 2026-10-14T23:48:16Z

> Ruling (kernel-red-2), 1 of 2: the mechanism. Read: consoled server.rs Lines::write + write (prefix and body go out inside ONE console_held chunk), rt console_held (a refused Take writes anyway, silently), kernel console.rs (held: queued; Release flushes 'before the holder's next write'), device.rs check_console, init.rs, B57's rerun log (smp 1).
> 
> With the hold working, the observed bytes are impossible. They are possible in exactly two ways, both CONW1's: (1) consoled's Take is refused (Busy/WrongObject) and it writes unprotected, so a kernel entry between the prefix's and the body's MMIO writes prints free; (2) the body's first byte is a short write (put_all 0 after the 23-byte prefix): Lines leaves the line open with its prefix out, consoled releases, the kernel flushes the queued fall line right there, and the client's retry writes the body with no prefix. The smp-1 failure and the determinism point at (1) or an icount-deterministic (2); a probe decides, not a guess.
> 
> Review miss: both rounds judged the lines 'bounded and shown by containment' against the hold's chunk model and did not ask what a refused Take or a short write does to an open line. Mine too.

### kernel-red-2 · Answer

Event: `b5850bba9d0bf3250eda757ef3f608d9` · 2026-10-14T23:48:16Z

> Ruling 2 of 2.
> 
> (a) The fix belongs in CONW1's mechanism (consoled + the hold), not in B57. Refused: the kernel waiting for the console's current line (it cannot see MMIO writes and never waits for user mode); a counter the bench reads (hides that any kernel line, a kill's, splits the same way). B57's line stays a console line.
> 
> (b) A separate package CONW2, which B57 needs; B57's code unchanged. CONW2: (i) probe first: consoled takes and releases the hold once at start and reports a refusal (exit code, named in consoled.md), and counts short writes on an open line, read in the failing case; (ii) the rule to make true: once a line's prefix is out, no kernel line goes out on it: a hold is released only with no line open, a short write keeping it until the retry ends the line or another writer's write does; the kernel's 4 KiB spill stays the bound (documented, unchanged); (iii) proof in the system image, consoled not a kernel program: the three failing beamlet cases green, plus a kill line forced during a session's continuous output at 2 harts; (iv) kernel/ABI edits only if the probe shows (1) is a kernel fault: Tier A then.
> 
> Note for CONW2, not now: lines over HOLD_CHUNK are split across holds by design, so a kernel line may still land mid-line in a long line; the docs say so.
